E01.assertion_read: Three actual launcher processes converge to one PID/generation, ready; launcher exit does not stop it. Reuse keeps generation; explicit restart changes it; stale stop rejected; DRAINED receipt/run marker agree; DB retained.
E01.limits: Actual disposable detached service, no provider. Launcher exit is narrower than terminal/dashboard closure with admitted work.

E02.assertion_read: Connector: three actual starts, exactly one started=true/PID/generation; late launch token refused; secret sentinel absent from context; restart/drain receipt agree; state/journal survive.
E02.limits: No remote Server/provider or registered Windows task in this process case.

E03.assertion_read: Alias paths and shared DB exclude; independent DB/home acquires; two real processes yield one owner and OS lock releases after actual death; loser never bootstraps/migrates.

E04.assertion_read: Old heartbeat cannot steal a live OS lock; stale/reused/unknown PID is not death proof; old generation release cannot erase new owner.

E05.assertion_read: Readiness correlates held OS ownership, generation, PID, instance and exact active/installed version; wrong endpoint does not become ready; race in owner metadata is rechecked.
E05.limits: Wrong endpoint tests use a controlled response. This is not the full occupied-socket startup campaign.

E06.assertion_read: Status is passive on absent storage; logs only coded bounded records with corrupt/secret lines withheld; Ctrl+C follow ends observation; default doctor does not vault/network/start; remote failure has no local fallback.

E07.assertion_read: Pending launch is durable and not repeated; explicit recover-start fences late child without bootstrap; changed receipt or live owner refuses; lost reply recovers same intent.

E08.assertion_read: Installed start calls native scheduler, not detached launch; known pending start not resubmitted. Edited/foreign task and context mismatch refuse without overwrite.
E08.limits: Task mutations are injected; native XML validation is not registration.

E09.assertion_read: Enable/disable exact owned definition idempotently, with no start/drain; active disable keeps generation; lost enablement reply reconciles only exact effect.
E09.limits: Injected scheduler, not real OS enablement/login.

E10.assertion_read: Saved execution context uses resolved paths and allowlist, no terminal secrets; supervised entry verifies lock/token and restores caller environment after foreground call.
E10.limits: Pure/injected context validation; service-user OS vault/PATH still requires its real campaign.

E11.assertion_read: Stop latches before canonical shutdown; pending drain does not start/restart/force Task Scheduler; stale generation cannot latch successor; durable same-generation receipt recovers lost response.

E12.assertion_read: Administrative HTTP/TCP drain returns pending, preserves owner/store/tasks and read/recovery channels; current authority required; repeated request keeps original deadline; observer cancellation cannot cancel recovery.
E12.limits: Native/provider doubles. The audit did not execute these reports again.

E13.assertion_read: Repeated install no duplicate; foreign/user-edited definitions preserved. Uninstall requires inactive/drained integration and retains DB/credential/context sentinels, then repeats without effects.
E13.limits: Injected task mutation; actual unregister plus usable foreground afterward remains unqualified.

E14.assertion_read: Upgrade requires reviewed source generation/context and DRAINED latest run, resumes every write boundary, recognizes exact lost native effect, refuses edits/downgrade/unknown runtime and never auto-starts/migrates.

E15.assertion_read: Two installed disposable environments: live apply refused; stop then apply preserves raw DB/ownership ledger; repeated apply no change; executable changes, saved config stable; restart new generation ready and drains.
E15.limits: Actual environment switch, same package/version family; no real registered-task update, historical migration rollback or provider.

E16.assertion_read: Connect --plan invokes inspect only; approve/reconnect invoke ensure_running; one probe/test/Finish and saved-profile reconnect. Lifecycle itself is injected at this CLI seam.
E16.limits: Together with E01 this validates composition, not a single real first-connect-to-detached-start execution.

E17.assertion_read: Explicit login review shares setup consent; declines preserve on-demand; partial install resumes without another model test/setup; remote operator cannot initiate local startup.
E17.limits: Review/install effect doubles; no real logon.

E18.assertion_read: Expired/exhausted remote grant renewal uses one committed issue/receipt after reply loss; old leases/session not migrated; explicit new work uses new grant. Rotation fences old keys/tickets/reviews; completed reuse preserves canonical binding and Finish.
E18.limits: Real loopback HTTP/WS/IPC and DaemonApp, synthetic native/provider, temporary vault. Does not prove OS-service restart or two physical hosts.

E19.assertion_read: Lock storage/failed bootstrap prevents readiness/bootstrap or releases both locks rather than declaring ready.
E19.limits: No all-migration-failure process matrix is asserted.

E20.assertion_read: Wait timeout only returns timed-out observation, no relaunch/stop; restart pending refuses new start.
E20.limits: Ctrl+C during actual connect needs a focused retained assertion; log-follow cancellation is not substituted for it.

E21.assertion_read: Retirement/preopen recovery refuses release while Core owns slots/resources and never reopens an already verified journal; limited synthetic-runtime recovery.
E21.limits: Not real OS crash/suspend or native provider recovery.

E23.assertion_read: Actual foreground process retains HTTP/owner until controlled inventory release after HTTP-first/signal-first shutdown; repeated requests preserve deadline; failed startup never force-exits.
E23.limits: Disposable process/simulated signal path; not actual user logout, Task Scheduler stop or provider survival.

E22.assertion_read: Canonical request decision CAS and transactional Finish/claim remain the reused authoritative paths.
E22.limits: Historical baseline passes; current source hashes are separate observations, not a claim of historical fixture byte equality.
